source.title: Interpreting Face Inference Models Using Hierarchical Network Dissection
source.authors: Divyang Teotia; Àgata Lapedriza; S. Ostadabbas

record.tranche_reason: It compares two methods for identifying interpretable CNN units and reports concept-coverage outcomes, bearing on whether better tools increase the share of interpretable units. It does not use the claim’s language-model neuron-pole audit method.
record.gate_note: The study measures CNN unit coverage by matching activations to concepts in a face-image dictionary. Only the reported coverage comparisons and explicit model-specific coverage statements are included. Task performance figures and results cited from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper on face CNNs. Its coverage numbers measure its own pairing method (Hierarchical Network Dissection) against Network Dissection. That is the study's own method compared with another, not a test of whether better tools reveal that units have one main job. The hierarchical method lets a unit pair with several concepts. Its global-concept thresholds sit only 0.05 above chance (0.55 vs 0.5 for gender), and the authors say this 'primarily ensures a high coverage'. They also say the comparison is 'not strictly fair'. Higher coverage therefore reflects a more lenient, unvalidated labelling criterion, not more interpretable units. No held-out check of the explanations is made. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors present Hierarchical Network Dissection and the Face Dictionary as tools to interpret face models and reveal dataset biases. They note that coverage is limited by the dictionary and affected by data and training. The paraphrase should add that the authors state the coverage comparison with Network Dissection is not strictly fair, since their method also counts global-concept pairings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CNN activation maps, a face-concept dictionary, and hierarchical probabilistic unit-concept matching; it does not test language-model neuron poles or validate explanations on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: Coverage differs by dissection method; the paper also reports lower coverage for FairFace and Beauty than for other tested models.

fits_no_version.finding: In deeper layers of ResNet face models, a multi-concept probabilistic pairing method labels about 70-80% of units with some face concept. Standard Network Dissection labels about 50-60%. FaceNet is excluded, and FairFace and Beauty are lower. The labels are not validated on held-out data, and the thresholds are near chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The share of CNN units assigned a concept label depends strongly on the pairing criterion (single vs multiple concepts, threshold leniency), not only on the network.

record.code_released: The paper says the source code is available via the Hierarchical Network Dissection GitHub link; URL not stated in the text.
record.problems: Interpretability coverage is limited by the Face Dictionary, and the authors state that coverage can be affected by concept distributions and model training. The paper reports coverage ranges for a group of models rather than separate textual percentages for each model. No uncertainty estimates for coverage are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Fig. 8 shows model- and layer-specific coverage, but the text does not provide values that can be assigned reliably to each individual model and layer. Other figure-only concept histograms and qualitative examples were not extracted as coverage results.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label rests on a comparison of the study's own method with a baseline method, where the new method uses a more permissive criterion. That is method performance, not evidence that neurons are cleaner than thought, so no verdict is given. The dissected networks are face CNNs, not InceptionV1 or language models.

rows.note: The paper reports this range for most of the non-FaceNet ResNet-backbone models; it does not give separate percentages for each model in the text.
rows.check: This is the study's own method's coverage, compared with Network Dissection. Coverage counts units paired with any concept, including multiple concepts and near-chance global thresholds, so it cannot show the V4 effect (rise in neurons with one main job). The subject is 'most' non-FaceNet models, read approximately from Fig. 8.
